newsitem.title: NORWAY: NYCOMED CONFIRMS INTEREST IN POLISH GROUP.
newsitem.headline: NYCOMED CONFIRMS INTEREST IN POLISH GROUP.

text.p: Norwegian pharmaceuticals company Nycomed ASA, which plans to merge with Britain's Amersham International Plc, confirmed on Tuesday that it was interested in buying a part of Polish state-owned group Polfa Poznan.
"We have shown some interest in the company," Eric Cameron, chief spokesman at Nycomed, told Reuters.
Cameron declined to comment on which division it was interested in or the acquisition sum.
On Tuesday the Polish daily, Rzeczpospolita, reported that the treasury ministry had shortlisted three foreign companies in a tender for at least 10 percent of state-owned drug maker Polfa Poznan SA.
The newspaper, quoting anonymous sources, named Nycomed as one of the companies, together with Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc and U.S. Bristol Myers Squibb Co.

Nycomed, a niche player in the pharmaceutical industry, is a worldwide leader in the development of diagnostic contrast imaging agents for X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), ultrasound and nuclear medicine. It also supplies a range of generic drugs and other products primarily to European markets.
The company, which used to be part of combined drugs and energy group Hafslund Nycomed, announced on July 1 that it planned to merge with Amersham International, the health and technology group.

The merged company, to be called Nycomed Amersham, will create a global group, capitalised at 1.8 billion stg, with a leading position in in-vivo diagnostic imaging agents and research-based biotechnology supply.
